Package io.mavlink4j.codec

Class FrameWriter

java.lang.Object
io.mavlink4j.codec.FrameWriter
public final class FrameWriter extends Object
The only class in this module permitted to construct an io.dronefleet.mavlink.MavlinkConnection — every other class reaches the wire through MavlinkLink/FrameReader/this class, never the library directly. This is the one-place library-swap seam: replacing the underlying MAVLink library only has to change this one file (and FrameReader's decode path).

Sequence numbering

"Owned per (link, our sysid, our compid), wrapping at 255" is satisfied by construction rather than by hand: this class keeps exactly one MavlinkConnection per registered link, built once in addLink(io.mavlink4j.transport.MavlinkLink) and reused for every subsequent send on that link. A MavlinkConnection's own sequence counter already increments correctly and wraps (the wire byte is naturally truncated to 8 bits during serialization) — since ourSystem/ ourComponent are fixed for this FrameWriter's whole life, "per link" is the only axis that actually varies, and one connection per link is exactly that.

Routing lives in the session

This class is the routed half of the codec: it sends to a named link (broadcast(java.lang.Object, io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkId)) or to a named link and address (sendTo(java.lang.Object, io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkId, io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkPeer, io.mavlink4j.PeerId)). It cannot answer "which link is this PeerId reachable on"; that needs the session's peer directory, which is why FrameSink — whose implementation resolves the peer and delegates here — is the public TX door.

    • broadcast

      public void broadcast(Object message, LinkId link)
      Sends message (a dialect message class) out link unconditionally, using that link's own MavlinkLink.defaultTarget() — matches the protocol's own broadcast dispatch path (spec: target_system == 0 is an unconditional forward, no learned-route check).

      Always unsigned: a broadcast by definition has no single intended recipient system to resolve a signing key for. The session's FrameSink upgrades this to a signed sendTo(java.lang.Object, io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkId, io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkPeer, io.mavlink4j.PeerId) when exactly one keyed system is actually listening on link.

    • sendTo

      public void sendTo(Object message, LinkId link, LinkPeer address, PeerId target)
      Sends message out link to one explicit address, bypassing MavlinkLink.defaultTarget() entirely, signed for target when SigningKeyResolver.keyFor(int) resolves a key for it (unsigned otherwise).

      This is the only correct primitive for a targeted message on a shared listen link. defaultTarget() is "whoever transmitted most recently", so on a fleet gateway — several vehicles pushing to one bound port, a normal production shape — a targeted send that trusted it would deliver to whichever aircraft happened to speak last rather than to the one addressed. For an ARM or a mode change that is not a routing inaccuracy, it is the wrong aircraft. The session's FrameSink resolves the intended peer's own last-known address from its peer directory and passes it here.
